title: On the Number of Subsequences in the Nonbinary Deletion Channel
summary: In the deletion channel, an important problem is to determine the number of subsequences derived from a string $U$ of length $n$ when subjected to $t$ deletions. It is well-known that the number of subsequences in the setting exhibits a strong dependence on the number of runs in the string $U$, where a run is defined as a maximal substring of identical characters. In this paper we study the number of subsequences of a non-binary string in this scenario, and propose some improved bounds on the number of subsequences of $r$-run non-binary strings.
